newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares up as Yeltsin readies for surgery.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares up as Yeltsin readies for surgery.

text.p: Leading Russian shares edged up on Monday after news that preparations for President Boris Yeltsin's heart operation had entered the final stage, traders said.
They forecast further growth in the next few days.
The Russian Trading System index of 24 shares rose by 1.07 percent to 180.54 on $9.49 million in volume.

Russian and Western doctors who met to discuss Yeltsin's surgery soothed markets by saying that the president was in good form for his planned heart bypass, even though they declined to set a date for the procedure.
"The market must have risen in anticipation that the operation would have a good outcome," said Mikhail Khaleyev, chief trader at Alfa-Capital, adding that buyers were mostly smaller, niche players.
Victor Pitaleff, a trader from Renaissance Capital, said he saw higher demand and that cautious selling from London had failed to spark a sell off.
Alexander Bobolev, from Ik Aton, forecast the market would rise three to four percent in coming days.

Murmanskelektro was the gainer of the day, with prices soaring to $7.20 after $5.40 on September 18 when it was last traded. Sverdlovskenergo rose to $0.280 from $.245 on October 31 when it last saw action.
Rostelekom nudged up to $2.62 from $2.54 at Friday's close, UES firmed to $0.0830 after $0.0814 and Gazprom was up to $0.430 from $0.423.
